rule: Superclass constructor calls (`super(...)`, `: base(...)`, `: this(...)`, PHP `parent::__construct(...)`, Ruby `super` inside `initialize`) → `Parent#<init>`, constructor. A Ruby `initialize` / PHP `__construct` definition's ID is `Type#<init>`. `self.m()` / `this.m()` / a bare call to a member of the enclosing type → `Type#m`. If `m` is defined only on a superclass that is in the scan, the callee is `Superclass#m`.
notes: `super(name)` and bare `super` inside `initialize` -> `Parent#<init>`, constructor (SPEC lists "Ruby `super` inside `initialize`"). `greet` is defined only on the scanned superclass User -> `User#greet` for both the bare and the `self.` form.
